title: Frankenstein: surviving draft and remembered beginnings
observation: The Shelley–Godwin Archive dates Notebook A’s drafting to August–early December 1816. In her 1831 introduction, Mary Shelley recalled rain keeping the group indoors near Geneva, ghost-story reading and Byron’s story-writing challenge in summer 1816.
researchStatus: Source scope reviewed; manuscripts not independently authenticated
sourceLocator: SRC-013: Notebook A opening paragraph; alternate composition overview, opening two paragraphs. SRC-049: Introduction, pp. vii–viii (rain, ghost stories and Byron’s challenge), signed 15 October 1831. SRC-014: opening origin narrative and The birth of Frankenstein.
uncertainty: Notebook A is not the lost first story or a record of the moment of conception. Its dates are an editorial reconstruction. The rain/indoors narrative is a recollection published in 1831, not contemporary weather measurement. These sources do not isolate weather as a cause of creative choices.
